name: MO-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+21 partisan lean makes it among the most Republican seats in the country
Incumbent Eric Burlison holds a massive financial edge ($1.7M raised, $962K on hand vs. $50K for Hesketh)
Prediction markets price Burlison at roughly 98% to win
No public polling; forecast rests on fundamentals, but all available evidence points the same direction
model.rationale: Southwest Missouri's R+21 lean, Burlison's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising advantage, and markets pricing his win odds near 98% all align, with no evidence suggesting a competitive race. The forecast sits slightly beyond the fundamentals-based estimate given the incumbent's financial dominance and the absence of any Democratic counterweight.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing Hesketh within single digits, or a major scandal or outside spending surge against Burlison, would be the first sign this safe seat could come into play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Missouri's 7th District is one of the most Republican-held seats in the House, with a partisan lean of R+21. Incumbent Eric Burlison is seeking another term with a commanding financial position: about $1.7 million raised and $962,000 on hand. Democratic nominee Missi Hesketh has raised roughly $50,000, and a Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets give Burlison roughly a 98% chance of winning. With no polling, uncertainty is somewhat elevated, yet every available signal—partisan lean, incumbency, money, and market pricing—points to a comfortable Republican hold. A Democratic upset would require an extraordinary shift well beyond anything in the current evidence.
